sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。
我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: Often in life, we find ourselves wrestling with a decision.
sentences.zh: 在生活中，我们常常会陷入纠结的决策之中。

sentences.en: And when we do, we tend to focus on the outcome of that decision.
sentences.zh: 而当我们这样做时，往往会把目光聚焦在决策的结果上。

sentences.en: How we'll feel once all is said and done.
sentences.zh: 关注一切尘埃落定后我们的感受。

sentences.en: Will I love my new job or will I miss my old one?
sentences.zh: 我会喜欢这份新工作，还是会怀念旧工作？

sentences.en: Should I move to a new city or stay close to friends and family?
sentences.zh: 我应该搬到新城市，还是留在亲友身边？

sentences.en: Will having children bring me joy or will they feel like a burden?
sentences.zh: 生孩子会给我带来快乐，还是会让我感到负担？

sentences.en: We do this with smaller decisions too.
sentences.zh: 我们在做小决定时也是如此。

sentences.en: Is this expensive vacation going to be worth the cost?
sentences.zh: 这次昂贵的度假值得吗？

sentences.en: Should I find a new preschool for my child?
sentences.zh: 我应该给孩子找一家新的幼儿园吗？

sentences.en: What major should I pursue in college?
sentences.zh: 我在大学里应该选什么专业？

sentences.en: Our minds fill with questions as we try to predict the best paths to take.
sentences.zh: 当我们试图预测最佳路径时，脑海中充满了各种疑问。

sentences.en: We make lists of pros and cons, weigh our options, get advice from friends.
sentences.zh: 我们列出利弊清单，权衡各种选择，寻求朋友的建议。

sentences.en: All this to make our future selves happy.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是为了让未来的自己感到幸福。

sentences.en: But in running these mental calculations, there's something we rarely consider about the future.
sentences.zh: 但在进行这些心理盘算时，关于未来，有一点我们很少考虑。

sentences.en: We might not be the same person when we get there.
sentences.zh: 当我们到达未来时，我们可能已经不是同一个人了。

sentences.en: Our future selves might think, feel, and value things differently than we do right now.
sentences.zh: 未来的我们，其思想、感受和价值观可能与现在的我们截然不同。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we explore one of life's trickiest questions.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，我们将探讨人生中最棘手的问题之一。

sentences.en: How do we make decisions about the future when we cannot anticipate who we'll be when we get there?
sentences.zh: 当我们无法预知未来的自己会变成什么样时，该如何为未来做决定？

sentences.en: Our lives are made up of experiences big and small.
sentences.zh: 我们的人生由大大小小的经历组成。

sentences.en: Some of these experiences flutter by, never to be thought of again, while others make lasting impressions.
sentences.zh: 有些经历转瞬即逝，再也不会被想起，而另一些则留下了深刻的印记。

sentences.en: At Yale University, the philosopher Laurie Ann Paul, who is known as L.A.
sentences.zh: 在耶鲁大学，哲学家劳里·安·保罗（Laurie Ann Paul），也就是大家熟知的 L.A.
保罗，一直在研究这些经历。

sentences.en: She's interested in how they inform and transform who we are.
sentences.zh: 她感兴趣的是这些经历如何塑造并改变了我们。
保罗，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Laurie, in the middle of the 18th century, there was a young man named John Newton in England.
sentences.zh: 劳里，18世纪中叶，英国有一位年轻人叫约翰·牛顿（John Newton）。

sentences.en: His life story captures one aspect of this idea that you've been studying for a while.
sentences.zh: 他的人生故事恰好印证了你研究已久的一个观点。

sentences.en: I understand he had a rather difficult upbringing.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，他的成长过程相当坎坷。

sentences.en: He was seen as a difficult child.
sentences.zh: 他被视为一个问题少年。

sentences.en: Yes, and an important thing is that his mother died when he was very young, and I think this
sentences.zh: 是的，很重要的一点是，他的母亲在他很小的时候就去世了，我认为这

sentences.en: made him feel very unhappy and very alone, especially when his father remarried and basically
sentences.zh: 让他感到非常痛苦和孤独，尤其是当他父亲再婚后，基本上

sentences.en: So his mother was religious, but after she died, John soon found himself not just turning
sentences.zh: 他的母亲是个虔诚的教徒，但在她去世后，约翰很快发现自己不仅背离了

sentences.en: away from religion, but turning against it.
He became what you might call a militant atheiSt.
sentences.zh: 他成了人们所说的激进无神论者。

sentences.en: Was his father a source of support, Laurie?
sentences.zh: 劳里，他的父亲能给他提供支持吗？

sentences.en: No, well, his father was distant and unemotional and was focused heavily on self-discipline.
sentences.zh: 不，他的父亲冷漠且缺乏情感，非常注重自我约束。

sentences.en: So I suppose this was his father's way of supporting him, but John did not find it helpful.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜这可能是他父亲支持他的方式，但约翰并不觉得这有帮助。

sentences.en: In fact, it alienated him both from his father and from other people.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这让他与父亲以及其他人产生了隔阂。

sentences.en: And his character also then started to deteriorate.
sentences.zh: 他的性格也因此开始恶化。

sentences.en: And he also, importantly, I think, had this kind of experience of despair where he blamed
sentences.zh: 而且我认为很重要的一点是，他经历过一种绝望，他总是责怪

sentences.en: others and wasn't able to kind of take responsibility for who he was and how he was behaving.
sentences.zh: 别人，无法为自己的身份和行为承担责任。

sentences.en: So at one point, he was recruited to join the Royal Navy.
sentences.zh: 后来，他被征召加入了皇家海军。

sentences.en: But even there, he was rebellious and got punished for it.
sentences.zh: 但即使在那里，他依然叛逆并因此受到了惩罚。

sentences.en: What do we know about his life at this point, Laurie?
sentences.zh: 劳里，关于他这一时期的生活，我们了解多少？

sentences.en: Okay, so I would say recruited is a good phrase.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我觉得用“征召”这个词很贴切。

sentences.en: He was press-ganged by the Royal Navy.
sentences.zh: 他是被皇家海军强征入伍的。

sentences.en: What happened was, I mean, so if you were press-ganged, then you were pressed into service.
sentences.zh: 当时的情况是，如果你被强征，你就被迫服役。

sentences.en: As he was, he had some background with the sea, so he was especially valuable.
sentences.zh: 由于他有一些航海背景，所以他显得尤为重要。

sentences.en: But he wasn't, obviously, interested in hard work.
sentences.zh: 但显然，他对辛苦的工作并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: And he wasn't a model seaman, shall we say.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们只能说，他不是个模范水手。

sentences.en: And at one point, what happened was he was traded, basically, to a slave ship.
sentences.zh: 后来，他被转手卖到了一艘奴隶船上。

sentences.en: The Navy ships will exchange one set of seamen for another.
And this is what was happening.
sentences.zh: 当时发生的就是这种情况。

sentences.en: He clearly wasn't a very appealing member of the crew.
sentences.zh: 他显然不是个讨人喜欢的船员。

sentences.en: So he got swapped into a slave ship.
sentences.zh: 所以他被换到了奴隶船上。

sentences.en: And this became then very formative for him because he entered the slave trade.
sentences.zh: 这对他的影响非常深远，因为他从此进入了奴隶贸易行业。

sentences.en: So he finds himself working in the slave trade.
sentences.zh: 所以他发现自己从事着奴隶贸易工作。

sentences.en: And I understand, even here, he ends up making lots of enemies among the other men working on the slave ship.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，即使在这里，他也和船上的其他人结下了不少梁子。

sentences.en: So basically, he was just not a very pleasant person to be around.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他就是个很难相处的人。

sentences.en: I mean, well, for someone who doesn't want to be where they are, who doesn't have any kind of religious, shall we say, belief or faith to guide them, who I think is alienated,
sentences.zh: 对于一个不想待在原地、没有任何宗教信仰来指引自己、而且我认为内心疏离、

sentences.en: unhappy, it's really no surprise that he was completely miserable.
sentences.zh: 不快乐的人来说，他感到无比痛苦也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: And then he also started to have serious health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 而且后来他还出现了严重的健康问题。

sentences.en: So I think this added a certain kind of difficulty to his life.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这让他的生活变得更加艰难。

sentences.en: So at one point, John Newton gets left on the coast of Africa, and even the slave ship that he was on basically abandons him.
sentences.zh: 后来，约翰·牛顿被丢在了非洲海岸，甚至连他所在的奴隶船也基本上抛弃了他。

sentences.en: He goes through various experiences and adventures, but eventually finds himself back on a ship bound for England.
sentences.zh: 他经历了各种磨难和冒险，但最终还是回到了开往英国的船上。

sentences.en: But far from being grateful to his rescuers, he spends his days on the ship cursing and drinking, and at one point even falls into the ocean and has to be rescued.
sentences.zh: 但他对救命恩人毫无感激之情，在船上整天咒骂、酗酒，甚至有一次掉进海里，不得不被人救起。

sentences.en: So he's rescued, but that's right.
sentences.zh: 所以他被救了，确实如此。

sentences.en: He's not even, he hasn't repented, right?
sentences.zh: 他甚至还没有悔改，对吧？

sentences.en: He's, even though he had a difficult time in Africa, he was badly treated, got himself into trouble.
sentences.zh: 尽管他在非洲过得很艰难，受到虐待，还惹了麻烦。

sentences.en: And in general, he sort of just went back to his old ways.
sentences.zh: 但他基本上还是回到了老样子。

sentences.en: And even this kind of, you know, near miss didn't seem to have a significant effect.
sentences.zh: 甚至这种死里逃生的经历似乎也没对他产生什么重大影响。

sentences.en: On March 10, 1748, John Newton woke up in the night to find the ship was caught in a terrible storm.
sentences.zh: 1748年3月10日，约翰·牛顿在深夜醒来，发现船正陷入一场可怕的风暴中。

sentences.en: Well, okay, so a detail was that he happened to have with him a devotional text called The Imitation of Christ, and he had been reading it, okay?
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一个细节是，他随身带着一本名为《效法基督》（The Imitation of Christ）的灵修书，他一直在读它，明白吗？

sentences.en: And this is before the storm, so this was something that he'd been reading as he was traveling.
sentences.zh: 这是在风暴之前，是他旅行时一直在读的东西。

sentences.en: And then in the middle of the storm, right, he suddenly had the realization that, you know, not only was his, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后在风暴中，他突然意识到，不仅是他的

sentences.en: his life in danger and the life of the entire crew was in danger, it was this incredibly intense situation.
sentences.zh: 生命危在旦夕，全船人的生命也危在旦夕，那是一个极其紧张的时刻。

sentences.en: But he realized that if there was a God, he could expect no mercy.
sentences.zh: 但他意识到，如果真有上帝，他将得不到任何怜悯。

sentences.en: And so he realized, you know, at the heart of this, like, incredibly frightening situation where, you know, imagine a small, basically wooden boat being tossed around the sea with,
sentences.zh: 他意识到，在这场极其恐怖的境遇核心——想象一下，一艘简陋的木船在海上颠簸，

sentences.en: you know, incredibly huge waves towering over it, looking like, you know, knowing that at any moment death could come.
sentences.zh: 巨大的海浪在头顶翻涌，你知道死亡随时可能降临。

sentences.en: And then, you know, at that moment, you realize that you're in a position of vulnerability, and I think someone with religious faith would then look to God as a protector,
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，你意识到自己是多么脆弱。我想，有宗教信仰的人会把上帝视为保护者，

sentences.en: and he realized both in that moment that he truly was vulnerable, but given his past life and his past way of being, that even in this moment of vulnerability, you know,
sentences.zh: 而他意识到，在那一刻他确实很脆弱，但鉴于他过去的生活和为人方式，即使在这一脆弱时刻，

sentences.en: he didn't deserve the kind of mercy that God would provide.
sentences.zh: 他也不配得到上帝的怜悯。

sentences.en: The story goes that he and the captain of the ship had been plugging a hole, and this was after they'd plugged many holes.
sentences.zh: 故事说，他和船长一直在堵船上的漏洞，这已经是在他们堵住许多漏洞之后了。

sentences.en: But when they plugged this one, at one point, he says, if this will not do, the Lord have mercy on us.
sentences.zh: 但当他们堵住这个漏洞时，他突然说：“如果这都不行，愿主怜悯我们。”

sentences.en: And of course, at that point, he starts to reflect on the fact that he has, you know, railed against God for these many years,
sentences.zh: 当然，在那一刻，他开始反思自己多年来一直

sentences.en: and what mercy could a sinner like him actually expect?
sentences.zh: 咒骂上帝的事实，像他这样的罪人还能指望得到什么怜悯呢？

sentences.en: So I think it's like, I think it's a combination of, you know, the realizing that, wait, I'm in trouble, but also for the first time,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，这既是因为意识到“糟了，我有麻烦了”，也是第一次

sentences.en: maybe kind of comprehending what what vulnerability requires.
sentences.zh: 领悟到脆弱意味着什么。

sentences.en: Seems to me that in this particular context, he was able, maybe for the first time to realize what real vulnerability implied,
sentences.zh: 在我看来，在这种特定的背景下，他可能第一次意识到真正的脆弱意味着什么，

sentences.en: and also what the promise of being saved from that entailed.
sentences.zh: 以及被拯救的承诺意味着什么。

sentences.en: In other words, he was able to kind of see the appeal of religious belief, maybe for the first time.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他可能第一次看到了宗教信仰的吸引力。

sentences.en: Did the ship survive the storm?
sentences.zh: 船在风暴中幸存下来了吗？

sentences.en: So it did survive, but I think an important element of that survival came from Newton, because he took the helm for many hours, and for, you know, most of a day,
sentences.zh: 幸存下来了，但我认为幸存的一个重要因素来自牛顿，因为他掌舵了许多小时，几乎是一整天，

sentences.en: and used this time, apparently, as he was basically attempting to kind of, you know, having the ship respond to, like, to the waves and dealing with all the problems of the storm,
sentences.zh: 他利用这段时间，显然是在试图让船只应对海浪，处理风暴带来的所有问题，

sentences.en: also reflected on his situation and who he was and what he was doing, what he had done, his past immorality, his past behavior,
sentences.zh: 同时也反思了自己的处境、自己的为人、自己的所作所为、过去的堕落、过去的行为，

sentences.en: the way that he had isolated himself from other people, and really had a bit of an existential crisis.
sentences.zh: 以及他与他人隔绝的方式，这让他经历了一场存在主义危机。

sentences.en: As the storm subsided, he, I think, sort of also kind of emotionally collapsed.
sentences.zh: 随着风暴平息，我想他在情感上也崩溃了。

sentences.en: So the battered ship arrives in Ireland, and only hours before a second major storm strikes,
sentences.zh: 这艘破损的船抵达了爱尔兰，仅仅几小时后，第二场大风暴就袭来了，

sentences.en: and in some ways convinces John Newton that God, in fact, answers prayers.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上让约翰·牛顿相信，上帝确实会回应祈祷。

sentences.en: And for the first time in many years, he visited a church and began to pray.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他第一次走进教堂开始祈祷。

sentences.en: So it seems like what happened was, after experiencing this intense vulnerability,
sentences.zh: 所以看起来，在经历了那种极度的脆弱之后，

sentences.en: and in the midst of that, recognizing the power of being saved,
sentences.zh: 在那种状态下，他认识到了被拯救的力量，

sentences.en: and, you know, sort of understanding, like, you know, what that really meant,
sentences.zh: 并且理解了那真正意味着什么，

sentences.en: and how in a moment of great openness you can be saved,
sentences.zh: 以及在极度敞开的时刻，你是如何被拯救的，

sentences.en: and recognizing that is, in some sense, as, you know, the appeal of ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 并认识到这在某种意义上就是基督的吸引力。

sentences.en: So I think he interprets this.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他是这样解读的。

sentences.en: It seems like he interpreted this as a moment of insight.
sentences.zh: 他似乎把这看作是一个顿悟的时刻。

sentences.en: Then he was allowed to then return to land and survive.
sentences.zh: 然后他获准回到陆地并活了下来。

sentences.en: And the ship gets back just before, like, you know, a second huge storm.
sentences.zh: 船在第二场大风暴来临前及时赶回。

sentences.en: So he feels like there was a sequence where he experienced a kind of openness
sentences.zh: 所以他觉得这是一个连续的过程，他经历了一种敞开，

sentences.en: and a recognition of the divine kind of power and grace of God.
sentences.zh: 并认识到了上帝神圣的力量和恩典。

sentences.en: God grants him then the opportunity to survive by getting him to land in time.
sentences.zh: 上帝随后通过让他及时靠岸，给予了他生存的机会。

sentences.en: After that, basically, he starts going to church and kind of performing devotional services.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，他基本上就开始去教堂，进行各种灵修活动。

sentences.en: So in 1772, this was a little more than two decades after that storm at sea,
sentences.zh: 所以1772年，也就是那场海上风暴过去二十多年后，

sentences.en: John Newton writes a hymn to describe his own transformation.
sentences.zh: 约翰·牛顿写了一首赞美诗来描述自己的转变。

sentences.en: Many of our listeners have heard this hymn, Laurie.
sentences.zh: 劳里，我们的许多听众都听过这首赞美诗。
这首赞美诗开头是这样的，

sentences.en: And so you see it here, right?
So here's this description, basically, of someone who's finding themselves really in a pit of despair,
sentences.zh: 这里描述了一个人发现自己深陷绝望的深渊，

sentences.en: in darkness and lost and who's gone through great, great pain,
sentences.zh: 身处黑暗，迷失方向，经历了巨大的痛苦，

sentences.en: and then suddenly is relieved from this fear
sentences.zh: 然后突然从这种恐惧中解脱出来，

sentences.en: and can see the beauty of what protection and love and goodness could bring.
sentences.zh: 并看到了保护、爱和善良所能带来的美好。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, Laurie, what the young John Newton,
sentences.zh: 劳里，我很好奇，年轻时的约翰·牛顿，

sentences.en: the rebellious man who was always cursing God and drinking himself senseless,
sentences.zh: 那个总是咒骂上帝、喝得烂醉如泥的叛逆男人，

sentences.en: what would he make of the older John Newton,
sentences.zh: 会如何看待年老的约翰·牛顿，

sentences.en: the man we all now remember as the creator of Amazing Grace?
sentences.zh: 那个我们现在都记得的《奇异恩典》的创作者？

sentences.en: Well, I think this is something that's very hard for any of us to make sense of.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这对我们任何一个人来说都很难理解。

sentences.en: So anyone, certainly someone like John Newton,
sentences.zh: 所以任何人，当然也包括约翰·牛顿，

sentences.en: would view the future version of themselves
sentences.zh: 都会认为未来的那个自己，

sentences.en: that was kind of committed to a religious perspective
sentences.zh: 那个致力于宗教信仰的自己，
与现在的自己截然不同，

sentences.en: because the way that they made sense of reality
sentences.zh: 因为他们理解现实的方式完全不同。

sentences.en: is fundamentally how they can make sense of reality
sentences.zh: 这从根本上决定了他们如何理解现实

sentences.en: and I think would, you know, kind of reject that.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，人们可能会拒绝这一点。

sentences.en: You know, of course I wouldn't be like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我当然不会那样。

sentences.en: Another transformation that happened in John Newton's life
sentences.zh: 约翰·牛顿生命中发生的另一场转变

sentences.en: is that he spent some time in the slave trade working on these slave ships
sentences.zh: 是他曾在奴隶贸易中工作，在奴隶船上服役
但最终成为了一名废奴主义者

sentences.en: and in some ways led the movement against the slave trade across the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 并在某种程度上领导了整个大英帝国的反奴隶贸易运动。

sentences.en: Yes, this is another transformative experience
sentences.zh: 是的，这是另一种变革性的经历
